question.text: If a function $\mathbf{f}: \mathbf{R}-\{l\} \rightarrow \mathbf{R}-\{m\}$ defined by $f(x)=\frac{x+3}{x-2}$ is a bijection, then $3 l+2 m=$

solution.text:
$f(x)=\frac{x+3}{x-2}$
$\because \quad f(x)$ is not defined for $x=2$
i.e. domain of $f(x)$ is $\mathrm{R}-\{2\}$
$\therefore l=2$
Now, $y=\frac{x+3}{x-2}$
$x y-2 y=x+3$
$x(y-1)=2 y+3$
$x=\frac{2 y+3}{y-1}$
$y$ can take any value except $y=1$
Co-domain $=\mathrm{R}-\{1\}$
$m=1$
$3 l+2 m=3(2)+2(1)=8$
